exposure: Health-promoting lifestyle intervention (face-to-face education, pamphlets, phone contacts, text messages, social media)
Area for each member of family
cohort: The study included 350 reproductive-aged women with vaginitis selected from 10 health centers in Kermanshah, Iran in 2015, equally divided into intervention and control groups.
finding: The health-promoting lifestyle intervention significantly reduced the relapse rate of vaginitis (27.7% in the intervention group vs. 72.3% in the control group), with the control group having a 5.14 times higher chance of relapse.
mod_finding: Caesarean experience was identified as a significant sociodemographic factor affecting the relapse of vaginitis.
